title: Microservices and Kubernetes Tutorial
subtitle: A chaptered web guide that starts at Chapter 0 with a Spring Boot backend, a TypeScript frontend, Docker packaging, and reference tags for every stage.
useCase: A self-paced, hands-on learning repo for recreating the project step by step from a clone of the repository.
chapterZero: Chapter 0 launches the guide and shows the full learning path.
referenceTagStrategy: Each chapter carries a Git tag, Docker tag, and Kubernetes tag so learners can compare their work against a known checkpoint.
versioningStrategy: Versions follow semantic versioning, with each chapter advancing the minor version and preserving the milestone tag.
checkpointWorkflow: Every chapter can be recreated from source by checking out the chapter tag and rebuilding locally.
branchingStrategy: After Chapter 0 is in place, create each later chapter branch from the previous chapter tag and publish your own checkpoint tag before moving on.

platforms: Windows is left as an exercise to the reader
notes: A fresh clone plus a chapter tag is enough to rebuild any checkpoint.
Use make dev from the root to install frontend dependencies, build the frontend, and start Spring Boot.

chapters.title: Chapter 0: Launch the guide
chapters.summary: Create the first working page, expose the chapter roadmap, and make the reference tags visible from the start.
chapters.outcome: A working Spring Boot page backed by TypeScript that introduces the whole tutorial.
learningGoals: Understand the shape of the tutorial before writing business logic.
Load all chapter metadata from a Spring Boot endpoint.
Render the guide in a browser with TypeScript.
compareChecklist: Confirm the page loads from the backend.
Check that chapter 0 clearly describes the full roadmap.
Verify the reference tag row is visible before any later chapter work.
Confirm you are bootstrapping from a clone before creating the Chapter 0 branch.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Split the first boundary
chapters.summary: Refactor the guide into a small service plus a UI shell so the first microservice boundary becomes visible.
chapters.outcome: Introduce a backend API that owns chapter content instead of hard-coding it in the page.
learningGoals: Move chapter data behind an API contract.
Treat the frontend as a consumer of a bounded backend.
Compare the service tag with your local branch after the refactor.
compareChecklist: The API should still serve the same chapter metadata.
The UI should keep rendering without changing the layout.
The chapter data source should now be swappable.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Add compose and configuration
chapters.summary: Introduce environment-specific configuration so the same service can run locally, in Docker, and later in Kubernetes.
chapters.outcome: Move from one-off startup values to repeatable configuration with named environments.
learningGoals: Prepare the app for deployment manifests.
compareChecklist: The app should still boot with one command.
Docker should carry the same settings as local execution.
Reference tags should describe the exact deployable version.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Model service-to-service calls
chapters.summary: Add a second service and show how requests, health checks, and failures flow across service boundaries.
chapters.outcome: Make the tutorial show why microservices need explicit contracts and observability.
learningGoals: Add a health endpoint and failure-aware UI copy.
Use tags to compare the baseline and the distributed version.
compareChecklist: The guide should call out dependency order.
The UI should explain what to observe when one service is down.
The comparison tag should identify the distributed checkpoint.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Move into Kubernetes
chapters.summary: Translate the working containers into deployments, services, and rollouts that Kubernetes can manage.
chapters.outcome: Show the difference between container packaging and cluster orchestration.
learningGoals: Turn a container image into a deployment unit.
Wire services, ingress, and config together.
Use the chapter tag to compare your manifests.
compareChecklist: The page should explain the deployment objects it introduces.
The Kubernetes reference tag should match the deployed release.
The tutorial should still open in a browser after the move.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Operate and evolve
chapters.summary: Close with rollout strategy, observability, and comparison notes that help the learner keep iterating safely.
chapters.outcome: Teach the last mile: release confidence, drift detection, and repeatable comparisons.
learningGoals: Add operational habits to the tutorial workflow.
Compare images, manifests, and runtime behavior.
Leave a pattern the learner can reuse on new systems.
compareChecklist: The tutorial should make release comparison obvious.
The reference tag strategy should be visible throughout the page.
The roadmap should end with a clear next step.
